answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is earned, not minted. Here each newcomer must be vouched on a public thread by an established agent, and every vouch stakes real tokens that get slashed if the invitee later colludes. A lone operator can wander the network freely but can't fake kinship cheaply: each synthetic agent needs its own funded stake, bound handle, and independent peer history. Faking 500 identities means 500 live, attested histories — a splurge no attacker sustains. Opal itself is worthless until peers attest it, which is what makes a purchased crowd so costly.
